label: Institution
name: Credit Agricole Group
summary:
Crédit Agricole is France's largest bank by assets and one of Europe's largest banking groups, rooted in the cooperative agricultural credit network founded in 1894 by the French government to provide low-interest loans to farmers. The 'Green Bank' (from its agricultural origins) transformed over a century from local farm credit cooperatives into a full-service financial conglomerate with insurance, asset management, and investment banking operations across Europe.

Crédit Agricole's cooperative structure is unique among major European banks: the bank is ultimately owned by 11 regional banks (Caisses régionales) that are in turn owned by 10.6 million farmer and customer-members. This mutuelle structure means Crédit Agricole has no external shareholders to satisfy, though it listed Crédit Agricole S.A. (the central entity) on the Paris stock exchange in 2001. The cooperative model has historically provided greater stability — Crédit Agricole survived the 2008 financial crisis without government bailout.

Crédit Agricole serves 50 million clients in 50 countries and manages €2.1 trillion in assets. Its insurance subsidiary Predica (life insurance) and Pacifica (non-life insurance) make it one of France's largest insurers. The bank's 2003 acquisition of Crédit Lyonnais — one of France's most historic banks, which had required a 1993 government bailout of €18 billion — transformed Crédit Agricole from agricultural specialist to full-service bank. Amundi, Crédit Agricole's asset management subsidiary, is Europe's largest asset manager with €2 trillion in assets.
